description:
Follow-ups item 9 (with item 6's step 3, unit 3g): page URLs are paths, and links are plain (6c, 8).
- One page-path rule: GET /cms/{*page} (with /cms/ itself) serves the site's selected frontend for every path under /cms/ that is not /cms/api/ (whose routes and not-found answer are its own). An unknown path is the frontend's to answer. It replaces the /cms/edit/ and /cms/edit/{*path} routes; a file's page, /cms/edit/{path}, keeps its canonical redirect and its server-rendered page inside the one handler. With ?format=html, /cms/settings redirects to /cms/api/settings?format=html, and any other path is the server-rendered file navigation.
- The React built-in routes on the path (route.ts): /cms/, /cms/edit/{path}, /cms/settings and /cms/paint/{page} (the painting stays a query, ?painting=). ?view= and the /settings/ alias are gone.
- Its links are as plain as the path: each segment as written, with only a space, %, # and ? encoded (prettyPath; encodeURIComponent before). An ordinary file's link is its plain path.
- The contract's /cms/edit/, /cms/edit/{*path} and /cms/edit entries are one /cms/{*page} entry, the page-path rule. DESIGN-10 and DESIGN-11 name the new paths. The built-in's app.js is rebuilt.
